questions.q: A user has full record-level sharing access to a record and full field-level security on all its fields, but no object-level access to that object at all. Can they see the record?
options: Yes, because record-level access always overrides object-level access
No — object-level access is the first gate, and a gap there blocks the user regardless of the other layers
Yes, but only in Salesforce Classic
Only if they are a System Administrator
questions.explain: Security layers are not forgiving-additive: the user needs object access AND field access AND record access. A missing object-level grant blocks access even with everything else wide open.

questions.q: How many profiles can a single Salesforce user have?
options: Exactly one — it's the mandatory baseline
Zero or many, depending on their role
Unlimited, same as permission sets
One per object the user needs access to
questions.explain: Every user has exactly one profile, which sets the mandatory baseline for object/field access, page layouts, and login restrictions. Permission sets (plural) layer on top of it.

questions.q: What is Salesforce's long-standing guidance for granting app-specific access beyond a user's baseline?
options: Clone a new profile for every app
Grant 'Modify All Data' to every user to avoid managing access
Avoid permission sets entirely in favor of profile-only access
Keep profiles minimal and use permission sets (or permission set groups) for anything beyond the baseline
questions.explain: Profiles that accumulate years of object-specific grants become unmaintainable; permission sets (and permission set groups for bundles) are the preferred, independently assignable tool for extra access.

options: The default page layout assigned to a profile
The baseline record-level visibility (e.g. Private, Public Read Only, Public Read/Write) before role hierarchy and sharing rules grant more
Which fields are visible to a given profile
The maximum number of custom objects allowed in an org
questions.explain: OWD sets the record-level starting point. Role hierarchy and sharing rules can only grant additional access on top of that baseline, never less.

questions.q: A master-detail child object's sharing behavior relative to its parent is best described as:
options: Completely independent of the parent's sharing settings
It is always Public Read/Write regardless of the parent
It inherits the parent's sharing and can never be more open than the parent
It uses the child's own separate role hierarchy
questions.explain: A master-detail child inherits sharing from its master record, which is one reason Chapter 1's relationship-type decisions directly affect what's achievable in security design later.
